> Got it. Okay I don't foresee more than 20 users, and daily usage would likely be pretty sparse. Please provide an updated plan to allow multiple users that minimizes costs while also providing a fast, stable, and reliable user experience.

**Claude**

Here's the plan for up to about 20 occasional users. It uses no paid database: SQLite plus Litestream. Infrastructure stays at a few dollars a month, and Claude usage is the cost to watch.

**1. Sign-in and approval**
- Google sign-in stays, but any Google account can reach the app's front door. Inside, a new users table holds each person's status (pending, approved or blocked), their limits and when they last visited.
- Someone new signs in and sees **"Request access"**. You get an email, and they see "Waiting for approval" until you decide.
- An **admin page**, only for you, lists requests with Approve and Decline. For each approved user it shows spend this month, last visit, their limits, and a Block switch.
- Identity comes from Google's signed header, checked against Google's keys, so it can't be faked. Every page and API call refuses anyone not approved.
- You're the first user and admin, and your existing data becomes yours.

**2. Keep each person's data separate**
- Each person gets their own profiles, settings, documents, My Jobs, Jobby chats, scores, New & Noteworthy and usage log. Every query is filtered to the signed-in person, and documents go in a folder per person.
- **Sources are shared:** each person follows the boards and organizations they choose, and a board followed by several people is fetched once a day, not once per person. Jobs pasted in by hand stay private.
- Tests check every page, download and export to prove one person can never see another's data.

**3. Cost controls**

Sparse users matter here: the daily scoring costs money whether or not anyone looks at the results.
- **Only score for people who've visited recently**, say within the last 7 days. Someone who drifts away costs nothing, and resumes automatically when they come back.
- **A per-person daily scoring limit**, defaulting to 20 jobs instead of your 50. You can raise it per person.
- **A per-person monthly budget**, defaulting to $10. At the limit, Jobby, tailoring, discovery and "Ask Jobby" pause with a clear message, and you get an email at 80%.
- **Caching is already per person.** The scoring cache works within each person's run, so it keeps saving money with more users.

**4. Reliability: SQLite plus Litestream**
- The database moves onto the server's own disk, with every change copied to cloud storage within about a second. It restores automatically on start. This replaces today's riskier "database on cloud storage" setup, and the daily backups stay as a second layer.
- **Cloud Run settings:** still one copy (right for 20 occasional users and for SQLite), and the processor stays on while the server runs so copying never lags. With sparse use the server still shuts down after about 15 idle minutes, so this costs a few dollars a month at most.
- **One daily check at 2pm ET for everyone.** It fetches each source once, then scores per person within their limits, so 20 people take roughly the same time as one person plus their scoring.
- Memory goes to 2 GB so browser-based board reading can't run out while several people use the app. On Cloud Run's pay-per-use billing that's pennies.

**5. Speed**
- **First visit after a quiet spell:** the server starts in a few seconds, since the image is big because of the headless browser. Everything after that is fast.
- **If those few seconds bother you,** an always-on server removes them for roughly $10–15 a month more. I'd start without it and see.

**6. Email and trust**
- **Daily emails go to each person's own address,** from your Gmail. That's fine at this size: Gmail allows 500 a day, and it costs nothing. If you'd rather it not come from your address, a sending service needs a domain (about $12 a year) but is free at this volume.
- **A "Delete my account" button,** removing all of that person's data and files.
- **A short privacy note** at sign-up: what's stored, that it's sent to Anthropic's API, and that they can delete it.

**Cost picture**

| | Per month |
|---|---|
| Cloud Run, storage, Litestream | about $2–8, up from about $1–3 today |
| Claude, each regularly active person | about $5–20 with the defaults above |
| Claude, each inactive person | $0 |
| Worst case, 20 people all active at budget | $200, and the per-person budget enforces it |

**Build order** (each step deploys on its own, and your experience doesn't change until step 4):
1. Litestream and the server settings. Worth doing now even for just you.
2. Per-person data, with your data as user 1, and the separation tests. The largest step.
3. Sign-in, the approval flow and the admin page.
4. Per-person limits, budgets, scoring only for recent visitors, and the budget alert.
5. Per-person email, account deletion and the privacy note.

Steps 1–4 make it safe to invite people.

My assumptions, which you can change:
- shared sources;
- 20 scored jobs a day and a $10 monthly budget per person;
- scoring only for people who've visited in the last 7 days;
- daily emails from your Gmail;
- no always-on server for now.

## ab602548-080 · 2026-11-02 20:04 UTC

**Prompt**

> Let's set the scoring threshold at 3d rather than 7, and then add a last updated timestamp & refresh button to the New & Noteworthy page (let me know if you have any flags with that plan)

**Claude**

Both changes make sense. I have three flags, mostly about how they interact.

**1. With a 3-day threshold, email-only users would quietly stop getting jobs.**
- Someone who mainly uses the daily email and rarely opens the app would get scored for 3 days. Then scoring pauses, so the emails stop. With no emails they have no reason to come back.
- **Fix:** when someone's scoring pauses, send them one short email: "Your daily matches are paused. Open the app to pick them back up." Clicking it counts as a visit, and scoring resumes that day. It costs nothing, and anyone actually using the app never sees it.

**2. Someone coming back after a pause lands on a stale page.** If they return on day 6, New & Noteworthy shows nothing newer than day 3 until the next 2pm check. The refresh button fixes that, so I'd make it the obvious thing to do on return: "Last updated 3 days ago · Refresh".

**3. The refresh button costs money, so it needs guardrails.**
- **It shares the daily limit.** A refresh scores only what's left of that person's daily allowance. If the 2pm check already used all 20, a refresh still fetches new postings but holds scoring until tomorrow, and says so. Otherwise repeated clicks multiply the bill.
- **It has a short cooldown,** e.g. once every 30 minutes per person. Re-reading boards is free for Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby, but web-page boards cost a Claude call each.

## ab602548-090 · 2026-11-02 22:20 UTC

**Prompt**

> My account says my matches were last updated 3 days ago. That comes as a surprise - I don't know why it wouldn't have run for the past 3 days. Can you look into it? I was under the impression it was running daily at 2pm ET

**Claude**

I can't see your Google Cloud project from here because this environment has no credentials for it. I can't tell yet why the daily run stopped. The app's code isn't the cause, though: I ran the exact request Cloud Scheduler sends against a database set up like yours. It returned 200, scored the job, and recorded the run that "Last updated" reads. "Last updated" changes whenever any check finishes, including the 2pm one, so seeing "3 days ago" most likely means the 2pm run hasn't completed in that time. Either the scheduler isn't reaching the app, or the run is starting and then dying before it finishes.

Please run these in Cloud Shell and paste the output.

1. The scheduler job's state and its last attempt, including whether it's paused, when it last fired, and the result code:
```bash
gcloud scheduler jobs describe run-daily --project job-searcher-512814 --location us-central1 --format="yaml(state,schedule,timeZone,lastAttemptTime,status,attemptDeadline)"
```

2. What the scheduler saw on its recent attempts:
```bash
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_scheduler_job" AND resource.labels.job_id="run-daily"' --project job-searcher-512814 --freshness=5d --limit=10 --format="table(timestamp,severity,jsonPayload.status,httpRequest.status,jsonPayload.debugInfo)"
```

3. Whether those requests reached the app, and how each ended:
```bash
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND httpRequest.requestUrl:"/internal/run-daily"' --project job-searcher-512814 --freshness=5d --limit=10 --format="table(timestamp,httpRequest.status,httpRequest.latency)"
```

What I'll be looking for:
- **The job shows PAUSED, or there's no attempt in the last 3 days:** the scheduler itself stopped, and re-running `make scheduler-setup` or resuming the job fixes it.
- **The attempts show 401 or 403 and never reach the app:** the scheduler's sign-in through Google's sign-in gate (IAP) is being rejected, which points at its permissions or the IAP client ID it uses.
- **The attempts show DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, or the app's log shows a long or failed request:** my leading suspect. The scheduler job never sets an attempt deadline, so Cloud Scheduler waits only 3 minutes, its default, for the app to reply. A full daily run often takes longer than that. That alone shouldn't stop the run, but if the server shuts down after the scheduler gives up, the run dies before it records anything. The fix would be to let the app start the run in the background and reply right away, as the "Check now" button already does, and to set the job's deadline to the 30-minute maximum.
- **A 500 from the app:** a real error, and I'd want the full log entry for that request.

In the meantime, Refresh on New & Noteworthy will update your matches right now.

<details><summary>Claude's plan (approved)</summary>

# Multi-user Job Search Assistant (up to ~20 occasional users)

## Context
The user wants to open the app to other people while keeping costs low and the experience fast, stable and reliable. Expected scale: up to about 20 users with sparse daily use. Hard rule: nobody gets in until the user approves their join request.

Decisions settled in conversation:
- **No paid database:** SQLite made safe with Litestream. Postgres only past a few dozen users or if more than one server copy is ever needed.
- **One server copy;** sources shared across users.
- **Scoring only for people who visited in the last 7 days,** plus one "your matches are paused" email when someone crosses that line.
- **New & Noteworthy gets "Last updated …" and a Refresh button,** within the daily limit and with a cooldown.
- **Defaults:** 20 scored jobs a day and a $10 monthly budget per person, both adjustable by the admin. Emails go from the user's Gmail. No always-on server for now.

Where the app is today: single-user throughout. None of the 17 tables records whose data a row is. Nothing reads the signed-in identity; IAP admits one Google account. One SQLite file sits on a Cloud Storage mount with daily snapshots (D-019).

## NOW: Fix "StopIteration" killing every run (asked 2026-11-03)

**Context.**
- After the backup and scheduler fixes were deployed, Refresh still left "last updated 3 days ago". "Check every source now" then failed, and the Daily check card read `StopIteration:` with no message.
- Python raises StopIteration from `next(...)` with no default when nothing matches. The app has 6 such calls, each taking Claude's first text block: `preference.py:84`, `profile.py:70/131`, `app_insights.py:108`, `generate.py:313/386`.
- A reply has no text block when the model's thinking uses up `max_tokens` before it writes anything (stop_reason `max_tokens`). Here that's the preference rebuild: `max_tokens` is 1500 with no effort setting, so it defaults to high.
- The daily run rebuilds the preference profile for each person once enough new feedback has built up (`_maybe_rebuild_preference_profile`, threshold 5 new signals or 7 days). It catches only `LLMError`, so StopIteration takes down the whole run, everyone's included, before the person's `runs` row is written.
- The rebuild never succeeds, so it's retried, and fails, on every run: the scheduled one, Refresh and "Check every source now". That fits "last updated 3 days ago" and the 500s since Oct 31, which began after feedback built up. The FUSE errors were real too (and are fixed), but this is the likelier cause of the 500s and the one still happening.

**Fix:**
1. **`core/llm.py`: `response_text(response, action)`.** It joins the response's text blocks. If there are none, it raises `LLMError("Claude didn't return any text while <action> (stop reason: <stop_reason>)")`. The 6 `next(...)` sites use it, so an empty reply becomes the clean, catchable error every route and the pipeline already handle.
2. **Room to answer:**
   - the preference rebuild gets `max_tokens` 4000 and `output_config.effort` "low" (it's summarizing marks, not reasoning);
   - the profile build/revise go to 4000 with effort "medium";
   - app insights goes from 1500 to 3000;
   - the plain-text generation fallbacks keep their 3000-4000.
3. **One person's problem never sinks the whole run:**
   - `_run_for_person()`'s preference rebuild catches any `Exception` (logged, noted in that person's errors);
   - `_run_daily()` runs each person inside `try/except Exception`: the error is recorded in the summary's `errors` and a `runs` row is still written for them, then the next person runs;
   - a failure in shared work (polling, backups) still fails the run, as now.
4. **Better error text on the Daily check card:** `_system_run_finished` stores `Type: message (file.py:line in function)` from the traceback's last frame, so an empty-message exception like this one says where it happened. The full traceback is logged (`logger.exception`).

**Tests:**
- `response_text` with no text block raises `LLMError`, and with text it returns it;
- a preference rebuild whose fake reply has only a thinking block doesn't crash the run: the person is still scored, a `runs` row is written, and "Last updated" moves;
- one person whose processing raises still lets the next person's run complete;
- the stored error includes the file and line.

**Verification:**
- pytest gated on its exit status, ruff;
- after deploy, the user's Refresh should update "Last updated", and the Admin card should show OK;
- the existing app-log command shows the next 2pm result.

## Step 6, email and trust — DONE (deployed)

**Already done in earlier steps:**
- each person's daily email goes to their own sign-in address (`email_digest._recipient`);
- the approval, paused and budget emails;
- the privacy note on the request page (`AccessPage.PrivacyNote`).

**What's left: deleting an account, plus the privacy note in Settings.**

**Backend:**
- `core/reset.py`:
  - `delete_all_data(user_id=None)` takes an explicit person; it defaults to the current one, as now.
  - New `delete_account(user_id)`:
    1. take a snapshot (`"before-account-delete"`);
    2. run `delete_all_data`'s per-person deletion (rows, follows, pasted jobs, files), sharing one helper so there's a single snapshot;
    3. remove their remaining `settings` rows;
    4. keep their `llm_calls` as spend history, but anonymized: `user_id` set to NULL, with the note prefixed "deleted account";

  - `DELETE /api/admin/users/{id}` with `{"confirm": "DELETE"}`, admin only. It refuses for the admin's own account, and it emails the person "Your Job Search Assistant account was deleted".

**Already in place from steps 2-3:**

**1. Score only people active in the last 7 days.**

  - Active means approved and `COALESCE(last_seen_at, decided_at, created_at)` within 7 days, so a brand-new or just-migrated person counts until their first visit.
  - It replaces `approved_user_ids()` in `daily_run._run_daily()` for the everyone run.
  - Polling then reads only sources followed by active people (`_poll_sources(user_ids=people)` already does this).
  - `only_user` runs ("Check my sources now", onboarding) are unaffected, since that person is active by definition.
- **The paused email** (`daily_run._send_paused_emails()`, called in the everyone run):

  - wording: "Your daily job matches are paused because you haven't opened the app in a week. Open it to pick them back up: <APP_URL>";
  - a send that fails or isn't configured leaves the column NULL so it retries next run;
  - `touch_last_seen()` clears `paused_email_sent_at` in the same UPDATE that records the visit.
- The admin is subject to the same rule; there's no exemption, since the admin visits anyway.

**2. Monthly budget per person.**
- New `core/budget.py`:
  - `spend_this_month(user_id)` sums `llm_calls.estimated_cost_usd` since `date('now','start of month')`;
  - `status(user_id)` returns `{spend, budget, remaining, over, exempt}`;
  - `class BudgetExceeded(LLMError)` carries a plain message: "You've used your $10.00 Claude budget for this month. It resets on Dec 1, or the admin can raise it."
- **Enforcement at one choke point:** `core/llm.py`'s `get_client()`, which every paid call site calls right before calling Claude (17 sites). When a person is set (`optional_user_id()`), isn't an admin, and is at or over budget, it raises `BudgetExceeded`.
  - Because it's an `LLMError`, every route already turns it into a clean error message, and the pipeline catches it per job.
  - Shared work (nobody set) is never blocked.
  - **The admin is exempt:** it's their own key and money. Their spend still shows.
- **Daily run:** `_run_for_person()` skips scoring (allowed = 0) when the budget is used up, rather than failing job by job, and the summary notes "budget reached".
- **Alerts to the admin, once per person per month:**
  - in `log_call()`, after the insert, when a non-admin person's month spend crosses 80% of their budget, and again at 100%;
  - tracked by two new `users` columns, `budget_alert_month` and `budget_block_month` (e.g. '2026-11'), added via `MIGRATIONS` ALTERs, since the live `users` table exists already;
  - the email reads e.g. "Bea has used $8.10 of their $10 Claude budget this month. Change it on /admin";
  - a failure never breaks the call.
- **Budget shown to the person:**
  - `GET /api/me` adds `usage: {spend_this_month, monthly_budget_usd, exempt, scored_today, daily_score_cap}`;
  - Settings' Usage card shows "This month: $3.20 of your $10.00 budget · Today: 12 of 20 jobs scored" (admin: "no limit");
  - the Admin page already shows spend against budget, so its "enforcement comes next" note is removed.

- **Step 1 is built, pushed and deployed.** After the deploy:

## Step 1: Reliability: SQLite plus Litestream (useful even for one user) — DONE
- **The database moves onto the container's own disk** (`JOBHUNT_DB_PATH=/tmp/db/jobhunt.db`). Litestream replicates every change to `gs://…-jobhunt-data/litestream/` within about a second.
  - The image entrypoint becomes `litestream restore -if-replica-exists` then `litestream replicate -exec "uvicorn …"`. Litestream runs the app as its child process and flushes on shutdown.
  - `litestream.yml` goes in the repo; the Dockerfile gets the Litestream binary.
- **One-time move:** the first start finds no replica, so it seeds from the existing `/data/jobhunt.db` on the bucket mount, then replicates from then on. The old file stays as a fallback.
- **Documents (`resumes/`) stay on the bucket mount.** They're written rarely and whole, which suits it.
- **The daily snapshots (`core/backup.py`) keep running,** pointed at the local database, written to `/data/backups/` on the bucket. They're a second layer of protection on top of Litestream.
- **Cloud Run settings:**
  - the CPU stays on while the server runs (`--no-cpu-throttling`), so replication never stalls between requests;
  - memory goes to 2 GiB for headless-browser board reading;
  - still `--max-instances 1` and min instances 0.

  With sparse use the server still shuts down after about 15 idle minutes.
- **Tests and checks:**
  - a local run with Litestream pointed at a temp folder: write, kill, restore, data intact;
  - restore, then confirm the app sees the same applications;
  - the snapshot code works with the new path.
- **Docs:** CLAUDE.md Deploy section, D-020.

## Step 2: Per-person data (the largest step)
- **New `users` table:** `id`, `email` (unique), `name`, `status` (pending / approved / blocked), `is_admin`, `daily_score_cap` (20), `monthly_budget_usd` (10), `last_seen_at`, `paused_email_sent_at`, `created_at`.
  - You are seeded as user 1 and admin.
  - All existing rows migrate to user 1, through a one-time migration, with a snapshot taken first (`backup.snapshot("before-migration")`).
- **`user_id` (NOT NULL, indexed) on every per-person table:**
  - `candidate_profile`, `preference_profile`, `settings` (key becomes (user_id, key)), `resumes`, `generated_documents`;
  - `applications`, `application_status_history`, `feedback`, `job_scores`, `scoring_queue`, `digest_entries`;
  - `jobby_threads` (uniqueness becomes per user + job), `llm_calls`, `runs`.
- **Sources are shared:**
  - `sources` stays global, deduplicated by URL or board token;
  - a new `source_follows (user_id, source_id)` records who follows what;
  - Manage Sources shows only the boards and organizations you follow, and "Add" or "Monitor" follows an existing source if one matches;
  - deleting a source stops following it, and removes the source itself only when nobody follows it any more.

  `jobs` stays shared for source jobs. Pasted-in jobs carry an owner (`jobs.user_id`, nullable) and are private.
- **Code:**
  - A FastAPI dependency, `current_user()`, gives every route the signed-in user. Every core function takes a `user_id`, and every query filters on it.
  - Files are stored per person: `resumes/<user_id>/…`.
  - Settings that apply to everyone (email sender, prompt-cache stats) stay global; per-person ones move to the per-user settings.
- **Daily run:**
  - fetch every source followed by at least one active user, once;
  - prefilter and score per user, round-robin across users, each within their remaining daily cap;
  - digest and email per user.

  The `_run_lock` and progress tracking become aware of who triggered a run.
- **Isolation tests:** a parameterized test signs in as user A and user B. B must get 404/403 or empty results from every endpoint touching A's data: lists, details, downloads, the CSV export, Jobby, documents, settings and insights.

## Step 3: Sign-in, approval and admin
- **IAP lets any Google account through** (`allAuthenticatedUsers`, via a new `make iap-open` target you run).
- **Middleware verifies `x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion`** (signature, audience, expiry, using Google's public keys, cached) and maps the email to a user.
  - Unknown email: a "Request access" page (name plus an optional note) creates a `pending` user and emails you a link to the admin page.
  - Pending users see a "Waiting for approval" page; blocked users see "No access".
  - Every `/api/*` route except the access-request ones requires an approved user.
  - Locally and in tests, a dev setting stands in for IAP, with a fixed signed test token; a plain header is never trusted.
- **Admin page** (`/admin`, admins only):
  - pending requests with Approve and Decline, each emailing the person;
  - users with status, last visit, scored today against their cap, spend this month against their budget, and editable cap and budget;
  - a Block switch, and a count of sources each person follows.
- **"Check every source now"** on Manage Sources becomes admin-only, since it runs the check for everyone.

## Step 4: Cost controls
- **Active users only:** the daily run scores and emails only users with `last_seen_at` within 7 days. Any authenticated page load updates `last_seen_at`, throttled to once an hour.
- **The "paused" email:** sent once, the first daily run after someone passes 7 days ("Your daily matches are paused. Open the app to pick them back up," with a link).
  - Tracked by `paused_email_sent_at`, which clears on their next visit. Coming back resumes scoring at the next run, or right away via Refresh.
- **Per-person daily cap** replaces the global `daily_llm_cap`, shared by the daily run and Refresh.
- **Per-person monthly budget:**
  - summed from that user's `llm_calls` for this month;
  - at 80% you get an email (once per user per month);
  - at 100%, paid actions (Jobby, tailoring, discovery, "Ask Jobby", Refresh's scoring, the daily scoring) stop with a clear message until the budget is raised or the month rolls over;
  - a one-line "budget used" indicator on the user's Settings.
- **Prompt caching stays per user** (the scoring context is identical within one user's batch), so step 2's round-robin scores each user's jobs as one contiguous batch to keep the cache warm.

## Step 5: New & Noteworthy freshness
- **"Last updated 2 hours ago"** from the user's latest finished check, daily or refresh, from the per-user `runs` table.
- **A "Refresh" button** that runs this person's check now:
  - fetches their followed sources, skipping any fetched by anyone in the last hour;
  - scores within what's left of today's cap;
  - adds to their New & Noteworthy.

  It streams progress like the existing check ("Reading 3 of 8 sources… Scored 5 of 12…") and has a 30-minute cooldown per person.
- **When today's cap is used up,** it still fetches new postings and says "scoring resumes tomorrow (20 of 20 used today)".
- **A user coming back after a pause** sees "Last updated 9 days ago · Refresh" as the prominent prompt.

## Step 6: Email and trust
- **The daily email goes to each person's own address** (their sign-in email), from your Gmail via the existing SMTP set-up (500/day limit; fine for 20). The approval, paused and budget emails use the same path.
- **"Delete my account"** on Settings: types DELETE, takes a snapshot, then removes all of that user's rows and files and their follows. Sources nobody follows any more are removed.
  - The admin can delete a user the same way.
- **Privacy note** shown on the request-access page and linked in Settings: what's stored, that resume text, profile and postings go to Anthropic's API, and that the user can delete everything.

## Cost picture (estimated)

| | Per month |
|---|---|
| Cloud Run, storage, Litestream | about $2–8 |
| Claude, each active person with defaults | about $5–20, capped at their budget |
| Claude, each inactive person | $0 |
| Worst case, 20 people all at budget | $200 |

## Order and deploys
- **Step 1 ships first,** on its own; you notice nothing but better safety.
- **Steps 2 and 3 ship together,** since per-user data needs an identity. Until you approve someone, it's still just you.
- **Step 4 then 5 then 6;** each deploys separately.
- **Invite people after step 4.** Steps 5 and 6 can follow while a few people are using it.

## Verification throughout

- Step 2: the isolation test suite. Step 1: a restore test.

# NOW: Scoring cost experiment (asked 2026-11-03)

## Context
- Scoring costs about 2–3¢ a job. Most of that is output: the model's reasoning at effort "medium" plus a free-length rationale. Postings are also sent whole (`core/scoring.py`'s `score_job`).
- The proposed lean settings could bring that to about 1–1.5¢:
  - effort "low";
  - a 2–3 sentence rationale;
  - the posting capped at 6,000 characters.
- The user chose to measure before switching: rescore 20 jobs they've already judged, under both settings, and compare cost and ratings. Nothing about live scoring changes yet.
- The production data lives only in the deployed app, so this runs there, admin-only, from a card on `/admin`. The experiment costs about 70¢: 20 jobs × both arms, so the comparison isn't confounded by the profile having changed since the stored scores.

## Backend
**`core/scoring.py`:**
- Add `ScoringSettings(effort, max_posting_chars, short_rationale)` with two presets:
  - `CURRENT`: medium effort, no cap, normal rationale, i.e. exactly today's behaviour;
  - `LEAN`: low effort, a 6,000-character cap, short rationale.
- Split `score_job` into `_score(job, *args, settings, note) -> (ScoredPosting, cost_usd, output_tokens)`. `score_job` keeps its signature and calls it with `CURRENT`, so the daily run and paste-in are unchanged.
- `LEAN` truncates `description_text`, ending with "…(truncated)". It appends one line to `SYSTEM_PROMPT` ("Keep the rationale to 2–3 sentences; still mark the 2–4 key phrases"). This sits in the first, uncached system block, so each arm still caches its own context.
- Cost comes from `llm.estimate_cost_usd` on the response usage. Every call is still logged through `log_call`, as `scoring` with note "scoring experiment: current|lean".

**New `core/scoring_experiment.py`,** modelled on `core/retag.py`: a lock, a state dict, `start()` running a `carry(_run)` background thread, and a 4-worker pool.
- **Sample:** up to 20 of the signed-in person's visible jobs that have a judgment:
  - a `feedback` mark (interested / not_interested); or
  - an application whose status reached interviewing/offer (counted as interested) or `rejected_no_interview` (counted as weak).

  Half positive and half negative where possible, newest first, and generic postings excluded. The description is backfilled the way `daily_run._backfill_description` does.
- **Run:** all 20 under `CURRENT`, then all 20 under `LEAN`, so each arm's cache stays warm within its batch. Scores are **not** written to `job_scores`, the queue or the digest.
- **Result,** saved in the `scoring_experiment` setting so a revisit costs nothing:
  - per job: title, company, your judgment, and for each arm the interest and fit labels and scores, the cost, output tokens and rationale;
  - summary for each arm: average cost per job and total; label agreement between the arms (interest and fit, % identical, and the average absolute score difference); and how well each arm agrees with your marks (share of Interested jobs rated High/Med interest, and of Not-interested jobs rated Low).

**`api/admin.py`** (admin-only router):
- `GET /api/admin/scoring-experiment` returns `{sample_size, estimate_usd, result}`;
- `POST /api/admin/scoring-experiment` streams SSE progress/done/error, the same loop as `api/settings.py`'s retag route.

## Frontend (`pages/AdminPage.tsx`, `api.ts`)
- A "Scoring cost experiment" card. It says what it does and offers "Run on N jobs (about $0.70)", with the spinner and "Scored 12 of 40" while it runs.
- **Result:** two summary rows (Current / Lean): cost per job, agreement with your marks, and how often the lean labels matched.
- **Detail:** a collapsed table of the 20 jobs (judgment, Current I/F, Lean I/F, a mismatch highlighted). Clicking a row shows both rationales side by side, so wording quality can be judged too.
- Once results exist, the button reads "Run again".

## Tests (`tests/test_scoring_experiment.py`, FakeAnthropicClient)
- `CURRENT` sends exactly today's request: medium effort, the full description, the unchanged prompt.
- `LEAN` sends low effort, a truncated description and the short-rationale line.
- The sample takes only judged jobs of the current person, and another person's jobs never appear.
- A run makes 2 calls per job, writes no `job_scores`/`digest_entries` rows, logs `llm_calls` with the experiment notes, and stores the summary.
- Only the admin can run it (403 otherwise). A failure on one job is skipped, not fatal.

## Verification
- pytest gated on its exit status, ruff, and the frontend build.
- A browser check of the card on the stub server with a faked client.
- Commit and push, prompt-log export, D-025 written once the user has real numbers.
- **The user** deploys, runs it once on `/admin`, and we decide from the result whether to switch live scoring to `LEAN` (a one-line change of the default preset).

# Multi-user Job Search Assistant (up to ~20 occasional users)

## Context
The user wants to open the app to other people while keeping costs low and the experience fast, stable and reliable. Expected scale: up to about 20 users with sparse daily use. Hard rule: nobody gets in until the user approves their join request.

Decisions settled in conversation:
- **No paid database:** SQLite made safe with Litestream. Postgres only past a few dozen users or if more than one server copy is ever needed.
- **One server copy;** sources shared across users.
- **Scoring only for people who visited in the last 7 days,** plus one "your matches are paused" email when someone crosses that line.
- **New & Noteworthy gets "Last updated …" and a Refresh button,** within the daily limit and with a cooldown.
- **Defaults:** 20 scored jobs a day and a $10 monthly budget per person, both adjustable by the admin. Emails go from the user's Gmail. No always-on server for now.

Where the app is today: single-user throughout. None of the 17 tables records whose data a row is. Nothing reads the signed-in identity; IAP admits one Google account. One SQLite file sits on a Cloud Storage mount with daily snapshots (D-019).

## NOW: Fix "StopIteration" killing every run (asked 2026-11-03)

**Context.**
- After the backup and scheduler fixes were deployed, Refresh still left "last updated 3 days ago". "Check every source now" then failed, and the Daily check card read `StopIteration:` with no message.
- Python raises StopIteration from `next(...)` with no default when nothing matches. The app has 6 such calls, each taking Claude's first text block: `preference.py:84`, `profile.py:70/131`, `app_insights.py:108`, `generate.py:313/386`.
- A reply has no text block when the model's thinking uses up `max_tokens` before it writes anything (stop_reason `max_tokens`). Here that's the preference rebuild: `max_tokens` is 1500 with no effort setting, so it defaults to high.
- The daily run rebuilds the preference profile for each person once enough new feedback has built up (`_maybe_rebuild_preference_profile`, threshold 5 new signals or 7 days). It catches only `LLMError`, so StopIteration takes down the whole run, everyone's included, before the person's `runs` row is written.
- The rebuild never succeeds, so it's retried, and fails, on every run: the scheduled one, Refresh and "Check every source now". That fits "last updated 3 days ago" and the 500s since Oct 31, which began after feedback built up. The FUSE errors were real too (and are fixed), but this is the likelier cause of the 500s and the one still happening.

**Fix:**
1. **`core/llm.py`: `response_text(response, action)`.** It joins the response's text blocks. If there are none, it raises `LLMError("Claude didn't return any text while <action> (stop reason: <stop_reason>)")`. The 6 `next(...)` sites use it, so an empty reply becomes the clean, catchable error every route and the pipeline already handle.
2. **Room to answer:**
   - the preference rebuild gets `max_tokens` 4000 and `output_config.effort` "low" (it's summarizing marks, not reasoning);
   - the profile build/revise go to 4000 with effort "medium";
   - app insights goes from 1500 to 3000;
   - the plain-text generation fallbacks keep their 3000-4000.
3. **One person's problem never sinks the whole run:**
   - `_run_for_person()`'s preference rebuild catches any `Exception` (logged, noted in that person's errors);
   - `_run_daily()` runs each person inside `try/except Exception`: the error is recorded in the summary's `errors` and a `runs` row is still written for them, then the next person runs;
   - a failure in shared work (polling, backups) still fails the run, as now.
4. **Better error text on the Daily check card:** `_system_run_finished` stores `Type: message (file.py:line in function)` from the traceback's last frame, so an empty-message exception like this one says where it happened. The full traceback is logged (`logger.exception`).

**Tests:**
- `response_text` with no text block raises `LLMError`, and with text it returns it;
- a preference rebuild whose fake reply has only a thinking block doesn't crash the run: the person is still scored, a `runs` row is written, and "Last updated" moves;
- one person whose processing raises still lets the next person's run complete;
- the stored error includes the file and line.

**Verification:**
- pytest gated on its exit status, ruff;
- after deploy, the user's Refresh should update "Last updated", and the Admin card should show OK;
- the existing app-log command shows the next 2pm result.

## Step 6, email and trust — DONE (deployed)

**Already done in earlier steps:**
- each person's daily email goes to their own sign-in address (`email_digest._recipient`);
- the approval, paused and budget emails;
- the privacy note on the request page (`AccessPage.PrivacyNote`).

**What's left: deleting an account, plus the privacy note in Settings.**

**Backend:**
- `core/reset.py`:
  - `delete_all_data(user_id=None)` takes an explicit person; it defaults to the current one, as now.
  - New `delete_account(user_id)`:
    1. take a snapshot (`"before-account-delete"`);
    2. run `delete_all_data`'s per-person deletion (rows, follows, pasted jobs, files), sharing one helper so there's a single snapshot;
    3. remove their remaining `settings` rows;
    4. keep their `llm_calls` as spend history, but anonymized: `user_id` set to NULL, with the note prefixed "deleted account";
    5. delete the `users` row, then their `RESUME_STORAGE_DIR/<id>/` folder.

  The admin's account (`is_admin`) can't be deleted.
- **Shared sources:**
  - a source nobody follows any more after the deletion is simply no longer read;
  - it isn't deleted, since its jobs may still be on someone else's My Jobs;
  - this is already how unfollowing works.
- **Routes:**

**Already in place from steps 2-3:**

**1. Score only people active in the last 7 days.**
- `core/users.py`: `ACTIVE_DAYS = 7` and `active_user_ids()`.
  - Active means approved and `COALESCE(last_seen_at, decided_at, created_at)` within 7 days, so a brand-new or just-migrated person counts until their first visit.
  - It replaces `approved_user_ids()` in `daily_run._run_daily()` for the everyone run.
  - Polling then reads only sources followed by active people (`_poll_sources(user_ids=people)` already does this).
  - `only_user` runs ("Check my sources now", onboarding) are unaffected, since that person is active by definition.

  - a send that fails or isn't configured leaves the column NULL so it retries next run;
  - `touch_last_seen()` clears `paused_email_sent_at` in the same UPDATE that records the visit.
- The admin is subject to the same rule; there's no exemption, since the admin visits anyway.

**2. Monthly budget per person.**
- New `core/budget.py`:

## Step 1: Reliability: SQLite plus Litestream (useful even for one user) — DONE
- **The database moves onto the container's own disk** (`JOBHUNT_DB_PATH=/tmp/db/jobhunt.db`). Litestream replicates every change to `gs://…-jobhunt-data/litestream/` within about a second.
  - The image entrypoint becomes `litestream restore -if-replica-exists` then `litestream replicate -exec "uvicorn …"`. Litestream runs the app as its child process and flushes on shutdown.
  - `litestream.yml` goes in the repo; the Dockerfile gets the Litestream binary.
- **One-time move:** the first start finds no replica, so it seeds from the existing `/data/jobhunt.db` on the bucket mount, then replicates from then on. The old file stays as a fallback.
- **Documents (`resumes/`) stay on the bucket mount.** They're written rarely and whole, which suits it.
- **The daily snapshots (`core/backup.py`) keep running,** pointed at the local database, written to `/data/backups/` on the bucket. They're a second layer of protection on top of Litestream.
- **Cloud Run settings:**
  - the CPU stays on while the server runs (`--no-cpu-throttling`), so replication never stalls between requests;
  - memory goes to 2 GiB for headless-browser board reading;
  - still `--max-instances 1` and min instances 0.

  With sparse use the server still shuts down after about 15 idle minutes.
- **Tests and checks:**
  - a local run with Litestream pointed at a temp folder: write, kill, restore, data intact;
  - restore, then confirm the app sees the same applications;
  - the snapshot code works with the new path.
- **Docs:** CLAUDE.md Deploy section, D-020.

## Step 2: Per-person data (the largest step)
- **New `users` table:** `id`, `email` (unique), `name`, `status` (pending / approved / blocked), `is_admin`, `daily_score_cap` (20), `monthly_budget_usd` (10), `last_seen_at`, `paused_email_sent_at`, `created_at`.
  - You are seeded as user 1 and admin.
  - All existing rows migrate to user 1, through a one-time migration, with a snapshot taken first (`backup.snapshot("before-migration")`).
- **`user_id` (NOT NULL, indexed) on every per-person table:**
  - `candidate_profile`, `preference_profile`, `settings` (key becomes (user_id, key)), `resumes`, `generated_documents`;
  - `applications`, `application_status_history`, `feedback`, `job_scores`, `scoring_queue`, `digest_entries`;
  - `jobby_threads` (uniqueness becomes per user + job), `llm_calls`, `runs`.
- **Sources are shared:**
  - `sources` stays global, deduplicated by URL or board token;
  - a new `source_follows (user_id, source_id)` records who follows what;
  - Manage Sources shows only the boards and organizations you follow, and "Add" or "Monitor" follows an existing source if one matches;
  - deleting a source stops following it, and removes the source itself only when nobody follows it any more.

  `jobs` stays shared for source jobs. Pasted-in jobs carry an owner (`jobs.user_id`, nullable) and are private.
- **Code:**
  - A FastAPI dependency, `current_user()`, gives every route the signed-in user. Every core function takes a `user_id`, and every query filters on it.
  - Files are stored per person: `resumes/<user_id>/…`.
  - Settings that apply to everyone (email sender, prompt-cache stats) stay global; per-person ones move to the per-user settings.
- **Daily run:**
  - fetch every source followed by at least one active user, once;
  - prefilter and score per user, round-robin across users, each within their remaining daily cap;
  - digest and email per user.

  The `_run_lock` and progress tracking become aware of who triggered a run.
- **Isolation tests:** a parameterized test signs in as user A and user B. B must get 404/403 or empty results from every endpoint touching A's data: lists, details, downloads, the CSV export, Jobby, documents, settings and insights.

## Step 3: Sign-in, approval and admin
- **IAP lets any Google account through** (`allAuthenticatedUsers`, via a new `make iap-open` target you run).
- **Middleware verifies `x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion`** (signature, audience, expiry, using Google's public keys, cached) and maps the email to a user.
  - Unknown email: a "Request access" page (name plus an optional note) creates a `pending` user and emails you a link to the admin page.
  - Pending users see a "Waiting for approval" page; blocked users see "No access".
  - Every `/api/*` route except the access-request ones requires an approved user.
  - Locally and in tests, a dev setting stands in for IAP, with a fixed signed test token; a plain header is never trusted.
- **Admin page** (`/admin`, admins only):
  - pending requests with Approve and Decline, each emailing the person;
  - users with status, last visit, scored today against their cap, spend this month against their budget, and editable cap and budget;
  - a Block switch, and a count of sources each person follows.
- **"Check every source now"** on Manage Sources becomes admin-only, since it runs the check for everyone.

## Step 4: Cost controls
- **Active users only:** the daily run scores and emails only users with `last_seen_at` within 7 days. Any authenticated page load updates `last_seen_at`, throttled to once an hour.
- **The "paused" email:** sent once, the first daily run after someone passes 7 days ("Your daily matches are paused. Open the app to pick them back up," with a link).
  - Tracked by `paused_email_sent_at`, which clears on their next visit. Coming back resumes scoring at the next run, or right away via Refresh.
- **Per-person daily cap** replaces the global `daily_llm_cap`, shared by the daily run and Refresh.
- **Per-person monthly budget:**
  - summed from that user's `llm_calls` for this month;
  - at 80% you get an email (once per user per month);
  - at 100%, paid actions (Jobby, tailoring, discovery, "Ask Jobby", Refresh's scoring, the daily scoring) stop with a clear message until the budget is raised or the month rolls over;
  - a one-line "budget used" indicator on the user's Settings.
- **Prompt caching stays per user** (the scoring context is identical within one user's batch), so step 2's round-robin scores each user's jobs as one contiguous batch to keep the cache warm.

## Step 5: New & Noteworthy freshness
- **"Last updated 2 hours ago"** from the user's latest finished check, daily or refresh, from the per-user `runs` table.
- **A "Refresh" button** that runs this person's check now:
  - fetches their followed sources, skipping any fetched by anyone in the last hour;
  - scores within what's left of today's cap;
  - adds to their New & Noteworthy.

  It streams progress like the existing check ("Reading 3 of 8 sources… Scored 5 of 12…") and has a 30-minute cooldown per person.
- **When today's cap is used up,** it still fetches new postings and says "scoring resumes tomorrow (20 of 20 used today)".
- **A user coming back after a pause** sees "Last updated 9 days ago · Refresh" as the prominent prompt.

## Step 6: Email and trust
- **The daily email goes to each person's own address** (their sign-in email), from your Gmail via the existing SMTP set-up (500/day limit; fine for 20). The approval, paused and budget emails use the same path.
- **"Delete my account"** on Settings: types DELETE, takes a snapshot, then removes all of that user's rows and files and their follows. Sources nobody follows any more are removed.
  - The admin can delete a user the same way.
- **Privacy note** shown on the request-access page and linked in Settings: what's stored, that resume text, profile and postings go to Anthropic's API, and that the user can delete everything.

## Cost picture (estimated)

| | Per month |
|---|---|
| Cloud Run, storage, Litestream | about $2–8 |
| Claude, each active person with defaults | about $5–20, capped at their budget |
| Claude, each inactive person | $0 |
| Worst case, 20 people all at budget | $200 |

## Order and deploys
- **Step 1 ships first,** on its own; you notice nothing but better safety.
- **Steps 2 and 3 ship together,** since per-user data needs an identity. Until you approve someone, it's still just you.
- **Step 4 then 5 then 6;** each deploys separately.
- **Invite people after step 4.** Steps 5 and 6 can follow while a few people are using it.

## ab602548-101 · 2026-11-03 14:41 UTC

**Answer to Claude's question**

> "Want me to add the 'skip unchanged board pages' saving? It reuses yesterday's postings when a web-page board's text hasn't changed, with no quality change. It's worth checking 'shared spend this month' on the Admin page first to see how big the saving could be."="Yes, build it (Recommended)".

**Claude**

I built the no-quality-risk saving: when a web-page job board hasn't changed since an earlier check, the app now reuses the postings from that check instead of paying Claude to read the page again. It's pushed to `claude/upbeat-hamilton-y05u73`, and all 355 tests pass.

**Why this one:** at 0.9¢ a job, scoring is already cheap. Board pages, though, were paid for on every daily check whether or not they'd changed, and each read sends up to 40k characters of page and gets back up to 30 postings.

**How it works:**
- Before calling Claude, the app compares the page text with the same URL's earlier reads. If it matches, it reuses those postings. The same text always gives the same postings, so nothing you see changes.
- Dates like "Posted 3 days ago" or "today" are ignored in the comparison, so a page where only the dates moved still counts as unchanged. Each posting keeps the date worked out the first time it was read.
- Any real change, such as a new posting, means a fresh read. A read that found nothing or failed isn't kept, so it's tried again next time.
- Boards that embed Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby already cost nothing to read and are unaffected.

I haven't measured how much this saves; that depends on how often your boards actually change. After you deploy, you can check it two ways:
- Test fetch on a board says "(unchanged, no Claude call)" when it reused a read.
- In the Settings Usage log, the `custom_board:` reads should become less frequent, and the Admin page's shared spend should grow more slowly.

```bash
cd ~/job-search-assistant && git checkout main && git pull && git merge origin/claude/upbeat-hamilton-y05u73 && git push && make deploy ADMIN_EMAIL=you@example.com
```

I left live scoring as it is; the reasoning and the experiment's numbers are in D-025. # NOW: Skip unchanged board pages (asked 2026-11-04)

## Context
- **The scoring experiment's result:** current scoring costs 0.9¢ a job, and lean saved only 6%. Scoring stays as it is.
- **The user asked for savings with no quality risk.** The best candidate is web-page board extraction (`ingest/adapters/custom_board.py` `_extract_postings`):
  - every daily run sends each board page's text (up to 40k characters) to Claude and gets back up to 30 postings (`max_tokens` 12000);
  - it does this even when the page hasn't changed since yesterday;
  - it's shared spend (`user_id` NULL), shown on the Admin page.
- **Fix:** when a page's text matches a previous successful read of the same URL, reuse that read's postings and make no Claude call. The postings are identical, so quality can't change.

## Backend
- **`schema.sql`:** a new shared table:
  ```sql
  page_extractions (url TEXT, text_hash TEXT, listings_json TEXT, extracted_at TEXT,
                    PRIMARY KEY (url, text_hash))
  ```
  - It's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so no migration is needed.
  - It isn't per-person, and `reset._wipe` lists its tables explicitly, so Start over and account deletion leave it alone.
- **`custom_board._extract_postings(text, source)`:**
  1. Hash `_fingerprint(text)`.
  2. If a row exists for (url, hash), rebuild the postings from the stored listings and make no call. The listings are stored rather than finished postings, so a changed `company_name` still applies.
  3. Otherwise call Claude as now, then store the listings.
  4. Prune rows older than 30 days for that URL.
- **`_fingerprint(text)`** is the text with relative-date phrases blanked ("3 days ago", "posted today", "yesterday", "2h ago"), so a page whose only change is dates shifting by a day still counts as unchanged.
  - A new posting always adds its title and link, so it changes the fingerprint and gets read.
  - Reused postings keep the absolute `posted_at` worked out on the first read, which stays correct.
- **The step text** says when a read was reused: "read the page as plain HTML: 12 (unchanged, no Claude call)". Test fetch shows this. Its re-render path calls `_extract_postings` too, so it gets the same reuse.
- **Kept the same:** the daily run's flow, the embedded-ATS path (no Claude call already), and every error path. A failed or empty extraction isn't stored, so it's retried the next day.

## Tests (`tests/test_custom_board.py` or a new `test_board_reuse.py`; fake client counting calls)
- Same page twice: one Claude call, and the same postings returned.
- The page changes (a new posting line): a second call.
- Only relative dates change ("3 days ago" → "4 days ago"): no second call.
- A changed `company_name` is applied to reused postings.
- Zero postings or an LLM error: nothing stored, so the next read calls again.
- The same text on different URLs: separate entries.
- Start over doesn't clear `page_extractions`.

# Scoring cost experiment (asked 2026-11-03) — DONE

## Context
- Scoring costs about 2–3¢ a job. Most of that is output: the model's reasoning at effort "medium" plus a free-length rationale. Postings are also sent whole (`core/scoring.py`'s `score_job`).
- The proposed lean settings could bring that to about 1–1.5¢:
  - effort "low";
  - a 2–3 sentence rationale;
  - the posting capped at 6,000 characters.
- The user chose to measure before switching: rescore 20 jobs they've already judged, under both settings, and compare cost and ratings. Nothing about live scoring changes yet.
- The production data lives only in the deployed app, so this runs there, admin-only, from a card on `/admin`. The experiment costs about 70¢: 20 jobs × both arms, so the comparison isn't confounded by the profile having changed since the stored scores.

## Backend
**`core/scoring.py`:**
- Add `ScoringSettings(effort, max_posting_chars, short_rationale)` with two presets:
  - `CURRENT`: medium effort, no cap, normal rationale, i.e. exactly today's behaviour;
  - `LEAN`: low effort, a 6,000-character cap, short rationale.
- Split `score_job` into `_score(job, *args, settings, note) -> (ScoredPosting, cost_usd, output_tokens)`. `score_job` keeps its signature and calls it with `CURRENT`, so the daily run and paste-in are unchanged.
- `LEAN` truncates `description_text`, ending with "…(truncated)". It appends one line to `SYSTEM_PROMPT` ("Keep the rationale to 2–3 sentences; still mark the 2–4 key phrases"). This sits in the first, uncached system block, so each arm still caches its own context.
- Cost comes from `llm.estimate_cost_usd` on the response usage. Every call is still logged through `log_call`, as `scoring` with note "scoring experiment: current|lean".

**New `core/scoring_experiment.py`,** modelled on `core/retag.py`: a lock, a state dict, `start()` running a `carry(_run)` background thread, and a 4-worker pool.
- **Sample:** up to 20 of the signed-in person's visible jobs that have a judgment:
  - a `feedback` mark (interested / not_interested); or
  - an application whose status reached interviewing/offer (counted as interested) or `rejected_no_interview` (counted as weak).

  Half positive and half negative where possible, newest first, and generic postings excluded. The description is backfilled the way `daily_run._backfill_description` does.
- **Run:** all 20 under `CURRENT`, then all 20 under `LEAN`, so each arm's cache stays warm within its batch. Scores are **not** written to `job_scores`, the queue or the digest.
- **Result,** saved in the `scoring_experiment` setting so a revisit costs nothing:
  - per job: title, company, your judgment, and for each arm the interest and fit labels and scores, the cost, output tokens and rationale;
  - summary for each arm: average cost per job and total; label agreement between the arms (interest and fit, % identical, and the average absolute score difference); and how well each arm agrees with your marks (share of Interested jobs rated High/Med interest, and of Not-interested jobs rated Low).

**`api/admin.py`** (admin-only router):
- `GET /api/admin/scoring-experiment` returns `{sample_size, estimate_usd, result}`;
- `POST /api/admin/scoring-experiment` streams SSE progress/done/error, the same loop as `api/settings.py`'s retag route.

## Frontend (`pages/AdminPage.tsx`, `api.ts`)
- A "Scoring cost experiment" card. It says what it does and offers "Run on N jobs (about $0.70)", with the spinner and "Scored 12 of 40" while it runs.
- **Result:** two summary rows (Current / Lean): cost per job, agreement with your marks, and how often the lean labels matched.
- **Detail:** a collapsed table of the 20 jobs (judgment, Current I/F, Lean I/F, a mismatch highlighted). Clicking a row shows both rationales side by side, so wording quality can be judged too.
- Once results exist, the button reads "Run again".

## Tests (`tests/test_scoring_experiment.py`, FakeAnthropicClient)
- `CURRENT` sends exactly today's request: medium effort, the full description, the unchanged prompt.
- `LEAN` sends low effort, a truncated description and the short-rationale line.
- The sample takes only judged jobs of the current person, and another person's jobs never appear.
- A run makes 2 calls per job, writes no `job_scores`/`digest_entries` rows, logs `llm_calls` with the experiment notes, and stores the summary.
- Only the admin can run it (403 otherwise). A failure on one job is skipped, not fatal.

## Verification
- pytest gated on its exit status, ruff, and the frontend build.
- A browser check of the card on the stub server with a faked client.
- Commit and push, prompt-log export, D-025 written once the user has real numbers.
- **The user** deploys, runs it once on `/admin`, and we decide from the result whether to switch live scoring to `LEAN` (a one-line change of the default preset).

# Multi-user Job Search Assistant (up to ~20 occasional users)

## Context
The user wants to open the app to other people while keeping costs low and the experience fast, stable and reliable. Expected scale: up to about 20 users with sparse daily use. Hard rule: nobody gets in until the user approves their join request.

Decisions settled in conversation:
- **No paid database:** SQLite made safe with Litestream. Postgres only past a few dozen users or if more than one server copy is ever needed.
- **One server copy;** sources shared across users.
- **Scoring only for people who visited in the last 7 days,** plus one "your matches are paused" email when someone crosses that line.
- **New & Noteworthy gets "Last updated …" and a Refresh button,** within the daily limit and with a cooldown.
- **Defaults:** 20 scored jobs a day and a $10 monthly budget per person, both adjustable by the admin. Emails go from the user's Gmail. No always-on server for now.

Where the app is today: single-user throughout. None of the 17 tables records whose data a row is. Nothing reads the signed-in identity; IAP admits one Google account. One SQLite file sits on a Cloud Storage mount with daily snapshots (D-019).

## NOW: Fix "StopIteration" killing every run (asked 2026-11-03)

**Context.**
- After the backup and scheduler fixes were deployed, Refresh still left "last updated 3 days ago". "Check every source now" then failed, and the Daily check card read `StopIteration:` with no message.
- Python raises StopIteration from `next(...)` with no default when nothing matches. The app has 6 such calls, each taking Claude's first text block: `preference.py:84`, `profile.py:70/131`, `app_insights.py:108`, `generate.py:313/386`.
- A reply has no text block when the model's thinking uses up `max_tokens` before it writes anything (stop_reason `max_tokens`). Here that's the preference rebuild: `max_tokens` is 1500 with no effort setting, so it defaults to high.
- The daily run rebuilds the preference profile for each person once enough new feedback has built up (`_maybe_rebuild_preference_profile`, threshold 5 new signals or 7 days). It catches only `LLMError`, so StopIteration takes down the whole run, everyone's included, before the person's `runs` row is written.
- The rebuild never succeeds, so it's retried, and fails, on every run: the scheduled one, Refresh and "Check every source now". That fits "last updated 3 days ago" and the 500s since Oct 31, which began after feedback built up. The FUSE errors were real too (and are fixed), but this is the likelier cause of the 500s and the one still happening.

**Fix:**
1. **`core/llm.py`: `response_text(response, action)`.** It joins the response's text blocks. If there are none, it raises `LLMError("Claude didn't return any text while <action> (stop reason: <stop_reason>)")`. The 6 `next(...)` sites use it, so an empty reply becomes the clean, catchable error every route and the pipeline already handle.
2. **Room to answer:**
   - the preference rebuild gets `max_tokens` 4000 and `output_config.effort` "low" (it's summarizing marks, not reasoning);
   - the profile build/revise go to 4000 with effort "medium";
   - app insights goes from 1500 to 3000;
   - the plain-text generation fallbacks keep their 3000-4000.
3. **One person's problem never sinks the whole run:**
   - `_run_for_person()`'s preference rebuild catches any `Exception` (logged, noted in that person's errors);
   - `_run_daily()` runs each person inside `try/except Exception`: the error is recorded in the summary's `errors` and a `runs` row is still written for them, then the next person runs;
   - a failure in shared work (polling, backups) still fails the run, as now.
4. **Better error text on the Daily check card:** `_system_run_finished` stores `Type: message (file.py:line in function)` from the traceback's last frame, so an empty-message exception like this one says where it happened. The full traceback is logged (`logger.exception`).

**Tests:**
- `response_text` with no text block raises `LLMError`, and with text it returns it;
- a preference rebuild whose fake reply has only a thinking block doesn't crash the run: the person is still scored, a `runs` row is written, and "Last updated" moves;
- one person whose processing raises still lets the next person's run complete;
- the stored error includes the file and line.

**Verification:**
- pytest gated on its exit status, ruff;
- after deploy, the user's Refresh should update "Last updated", and the Admin card should show OK;
- the existing app-log command shows the next 2pm result.

## Step 6, email and trust — DONE (deployed)

**Already done in earlier steps:**
- each person's daily email goes to their own sign-in address (`email_digest._recipient`);
- the approval, paused and budget emails;
- the privacy note on the request page (`AccessPage.PrivacyNote`).

**What's left: deleting an account, plus the privacy note in Settings.**

**Backend:**
- `core/reset.py`:
  - `delete_all_data(user_id=None)` takes an explicit person; it defaults to the current one, as now.
  - New `delete_account(user_id)`:
    1. take a snapshot (`"before-account-delete"`);
    2. run `delete_all_data`'s per-person deletion (rows, follows, pasted jobs, files), sharing one helper so there's a single snapshot;
    3. remove their remaining `settings` rows;
    4. keep their `llm_calls` as spend history, but anonymized: `user_id` set to NULL, with the note prefixed "deleted account";
    5. delete the `users` row, then their `RESUME_STORAGE_DIR/<id>/` folder.

  The admin's account (`is_admin`) can't be deleted.
- **Shared sources:**
  - a source nobody follows any more after the deletion is simply no longer read;
  - it isn't deleted, since its jobs may still be on someone else's My Jobs;
  - this is already how unfollowing works.
- **Routes:**
  - `POST /api/settings/delete-account` with `{"confirm": "DELETE"}`, for yourself. The admin gets 400 "the admin account can't be deleted".
  - `DELETE /api/admin/users/{id}` with `{"confirm": "DELETE"}`, admin only. It refuses for the admin's own account, and it emails the person "Your Job Search Assistant account was deleted".
  - Someone who deleted their account and signs in again sees the request-access page (no user row), so they'd have to be approved again.

**Frontend:**
- **Settings, Start over card:** add a second, separate action, "Delete my account…". It uses the same type-DELETE pattern as Start over (no `window.confirm`, per CLAUDE.md). The wording: "Permanently deletes your account and everything in it. You'd need to request access again to come back." After it succeeds, it does a full page load to `/`, which shows the request page. It's hidden for the admin.
- **Settings, "Your data" card:** add the `PrivacyNote` (exported from `AccessPage.tsx`) under it, as "What happens to your information". The note is adjusted to mention both Start over and Delete my account.
- **Admin page:** each non-admin row in People gets a small "Delete…" link. It opens an inline confirm: type DELETE, then click "Delete account".

**Tests (`tests/test_account_delete.py`):**
- B deletes their own account: their rows across `PER_USER_TABLES`, follows, pasted jobs, files and user row are gone; their `llm_calls` remain with `user_id` NULL; the admin's data is untouched; a snapshot was taken; their next request gets `/api/me` status "none".
- The confirm text is required.
- The admin can't delete their own account (both routes).
- The admin deletes B: B is emailed and gone.
- A non-admin can't use the admin route.

**Docs:** CLAUDE.md (the multi-user section's "Not yet" line removed; an account-deletion bullet added), D-024.

**Verification:** pytest gated on its exit status, ruff, frontend build, a browser check (Settings for a non-admin shows Delete my account; deleting lands on the request page; the Admin page delete), then commit, push and the prompt-log export.

## Step 5, keeping New & Noteworthy fresh — DONE (deployed)

**Already in place to reuse:**
- `daily_run.run_daily(only_user=)` and `start_run_daily(cap, only_user)` run one person's check (their followed sources, scored within their daily cap and budget). They stream progress over `POST /api/pipeline/run-daily/stream`.
- `api.ts`'s `runDailyNow(cap, onProgress)` and `runProgressText()` render the progress.
- Every person-run writes a `runs` row with `user_id` and `finished_at` (`_record_run`).

**Backend:**
- **`GET /api/digest/status`** (`api/digest.py`) returns:
  - `last_updated`: the person's latest `runs.finished_at`, from the daily run or a refresh;
  - `scored_today` / `daily_score_cap`;
  - `can_refresh`, `refresh_available_at` (from a 30-minute cooldown on the person's last refresh);
  - `over_budget`.
- **Last refresh time** goes in the per-person setting `last_refresh_at`, so it survives restarts and needs no migration.
- **`POST /api/digest/refresh/stream`** checks the cooldown and returns 429 with "You can refresh again in N minutes" when it applies. Otherwise it records `last_refresh_at` and starts `start_run_daily(only_user=me, fresh_hours=1)`, streaming exactly like `/api/pipeline/run-daily/stream`. The SSE loop is factored out of `api/pipeline.py` into a shared helper.
- **Skip sources fetched in the last hour:**
  - a new `fresh_hours` parameter threads through `run_daily` → `_run_daily` → `_poll_sources`;
  - with it set, sources whose `last_success_at` is within that window aren't re-read;
  - `_run_for_person` still queues and scores that person's jobs from those sources, using the jobs already stored (a new `_recent_jobs_for_sources(source_ids)`: active jobs of those sources seen in the last day), so a second person refreshing right after the first still gets scored;
  - this also covers jobs already found by someone else's run today.
- **When the cap is used up:** the run still fetches, and the summary carries `cap_reached: true`, so the page can say "Scoring resumes tomorrow (20 of 20 used today)".
- "Check my sources now" on Manage Sources keeps working as-is, with no cooldown. It's rarely used, and the daily cap and budget already bound its cost. Refresh is the main way in.

**Frontend (`pages/DigestPage.tsx`, `api.ts`):**
- Under the heading: "Last updated 2 hours ago · Refresh" (the button is disabled during the cooldown, with a tooltip "You can refresh again in 12 minutes"). Before any run, it reads "Not updated yet".
- While refreshing, show the spinner with `runProgressText()`, then reload the digest and the status.
- **After a pause:** when the last update is more than a day old, show a prominent card at the top: "Your matches were last updated 9 days ago." with a primary "Refresh now" button.
- **When the cap or budget is reached,** show "Scoring resumes tomorrow (20 of 20 used today)" or the budget message under the line.
- `api.ts`: `getDigestStatus()`, and `refreshDigest(onProgress)`, which reuses the `runDaily` stream reader with the endpoint as a parameter.

**Tests (`tests/test_digest_refresh.py`):**
- status before and after a run;
- refresh runs only my sources, and a second refresh within 30 minutes is a 429;
- `fresh_hours` skips a just-read source but still scores my jobs from it;
- the cap-reached flag;
- the endpoint is per person (another person's cooldown doesn't block mine).

**Docs:** CLAUDE.md (multi-user section: steps 5-6 now just step 6 left), D-023.

**Verification:** pytest gated on its exit status, ruff, frontend build, a browser check of the digest header and the refresh flow on the stub server (the run stubbed), then commit, push and the prompt-log export.

## Step 4, cost controls — DONE (deployed)

**Already in place from steps 2-3:**
- each person's daily cap (`users.daily_score_cap`, `daily_run.remaining_cap()`);
- `last_seen_at`, updated hourly by `users.touch_last_seen()` from `api/auth.py`;
- spend per person in `llm_calls.user_id`;
- `email_digest.send_plain_email()` and `admin_address()`.

**1. Score only people active in the last 7 days.**
- `core/users.py`: `ACTIVE_DAYS = 7` and `active_user_ids()`.
  - Active means approved and `COALESCE(last_seen_at, decided_at, created_at)` within 7 days, so a brand-new or just-migrated person counts until their first visit.
  - It replaces `approved_user_ids()` in `daily_run._run_daily()` for the everyone run.
  - Polling then reads only sources followed by active people (`_poll_sources(user_ids=people)` already does this).
  - `only_user` runs ("Check my sources now", onboarding) are unaffected, since that person is active by definition.
- **The paused email** (`daily_run._send_paused_emails()`, called in the everyone run):
  - for each approved, inactive person with `paused_email_sent_at IS NULL`, send one email and set `paused_email_sent_at`;
  - wording: "Your daily job matches are paused because you haven't opened the app in a week. Open it to pick them back up: <APP_URL>";
  - a send that fails or isn't configured leaves the column NULL so it retries next run;
  - `touch_last_seen()` clears `paused_email_sent_at` in the same UPDATE that records the visit.
- The admin is subject to the same rule; there's no exemption, since the admin visits anyway.

**2. Monthly budget per person.**
- New `core/budget.py`:
  - `spend_this_month(user_id)` sums `llm_calls.estimated_cost_usd` since `date('now','start of month')`;
  - `status(user_id)` returns `{spend, budget, remaining, over, exempt}`;
  - `class BudgetExceeded(LLMError)` carries a plain message: "You've used your $10.00 Claude budget for this month. It resets on Dec 1, or the admin can raise it."
- **Enforcement at one choke point:** `core/llm.py`'s `get_client()`, which every paid call site calls right before calling Claude (17 sites). When a person is set (`optional_user_id()`), isn't an admin, and is at or over budget, it raises `BudgetExceeded`.
  - Because it's an `LLMError`, every route already turns it into a clean error message, and the pipeline catches it per job.
  - Shared work (nobody set) is never blocked.
  - **The admin is exempt:** it's their own key and money. Their spend still shows.
- **Daily run:** `_run_for_person()` skips scoring (allowed = 0) when the budget is used up, rather than failing job by job, and the summary notes "budget reached".
- **Alerts to the admin, once per person per month:**
  - in `log_call()`, after the insert, when a non-admin person's month spend crosses 80% of their budget, and again at 100%;
  - tracked by two new `users` columns, `budget_alert_month` and `budget_block_month` (e.g. '2026-11'), added via `MIGRATIONS` ALTERs, since the live `users` table exists already;
  - the email reads e.g. "Bea has used $8.10 of their $10 Claude budget this month. Change it on /admin";
  - a failure never breaks the call.
- **Budget shown to the person:**
  - `GET /api/me` adds `usage: {spend_this_month, monthly_budget_usd, exempt, scored_today, daily_score_cap}`;
  - Settings' Usage card shows "This month: $3.20 of your $10.00 budget · Today: 12 of 20 jobs scored" (admin: "no limit");
  - the Admin page already shows spend against budget, so its "enforcement comes next" note is removed.

**Files:**
- `src/jobhunt/core/users.py`, a new `src/jobhunt/core/budget.py`, `src/jobhunt/core/llm.py`
- `src/jobhunt/pipeline/daily_run.py`, `src/jobhunt/db/connection.py` (MIGRATIONS) + `schema.sql` (the new columns)
- `src/jobhunt/api/access.py` (`/api/me` usage)
- `frontend/src/api.ts` (`Me.usage`), `pages/SettingsPage.tsx`, `pages/AdminPage.tsx` (note text)
- CLAUDE.md, DECISIONS.md D-022

**Tests (`tests/test_cost_controls.py`):**
- inactive people (8 days) aren't scored and their sources aren't read; active ones are;
- the paused email goes out once, and a visit (a request) clears it, so it can go out again after another lapse;
- a never-seen, just-approved person counts as active;
- a non-admin over budget: `get_client()` raises, a paid route returns the budget message, and the daily run skips their scoring;
- the admin is never blocked;
- the 80% and 100% admin emails are sent once each per month;
- `/api/me` reports usage.

**Verification:** pytest gated on its exit status, ruff, frontend build, a browser look at Settings' usage line, then commit, push and the prompt-log export.

**Deploy:** `make deploy ADMIN_EMAIL=...` as before. No new secrets. The new columns are added automatically at startup.
